penumbra.text: The partially shaded outer region of a shadow, as during an eclipse.

dysentery.text: An intestinal infection causing severe diarrhea with blood.

hornswoggle.text: To swindle, cheat, or hoax someone.

bamboozle.text: To fool or trick someone, often by confusing them.

flibbertigibbet.text: A frivolous, flighty, or excessively talkative person.

gobbledygook.text: Language that is meaningless or hard to understand, especially official jargon.

lollygag.text: To spend time aimlessly; to dawdle.

skedaddle.text: To leave or run away quickly.

brouhaha.text: A noisy and overexcited reaction or fuss.

kerfuffle.text: A commotion or fuss, especially one caused by conflicting views.

shenanigans.text: Secret or dishonest activity; silly or high-spirited behavior.

widdershins.text: In a direction contrary to the sun's course; counterclockwise.

collywobbles.text: Stomach pain or queasiness; intense anxiety or nervousness.

zeitgeist.text: The defining spirit or mood of a particular period of history.

serendipity.text: The occurrence of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.

petrichor.text: The pleasant, earthy smell after rain falls on dry ground.

defenestration.text: The action of throwing someone out of a window.

sesquipedalian.text: Given to using long words; (of a word) having many syllables.

pandemonium.text: Wild and noisy disorder or confusion; uproar.

quagmire.text: A soft boggy area of land; an awkward, complex, or hazardous situation.

snollygoster.text: A shrewd, unprincipled person, especially a politician.

gallimaufry.text: A confused jumble or medley of things.

lugubrious.text: Looking or sounding sad and dismal.

persnickety.text: Placing too much emphasis on trivial or minor details; fussy.

hootenanny.text: An informal gathering with folk music and sometimes dancing.

doohickey.text: A small object or gadget whose name one doesn't know or has forgotten.

thingamajig.text: A thing whose name one has forgotten, doesn't know, or doesn't want to mention.

whippersnapper.text: A young and inexperienced person considered presumptuous or overconfident.

scallywag.text: A person, especially a child, who behaves badly but in an amusing way.

ragamuffin.text: A person, typically a child, in ragged, dirty clothes.

hogwash.text: Nonsense; originally, kitchen swill fed to pigs.

gibberish.text: Unintelligible or meaningless speech or writing.

blunderbuss.text: A short, large-bored gun firing balls or slugs; an unsubtle and imprecise action.

cummerbund.text: A pleated sash worn around the waist, especially with a dinner jacket.

pumpernickel.text: Dark, dense, slightly sweet German bread made from coarsely ground rye.

rutabaga.text: A large, round, yellow-fleshed root vegetable; a swede.

kumquat.text: A small orange-like fruit with an edible sweet rind and acidic pulp.

zucchini.text: A green variety of smooth-skinned summer squash.

quinoa.text: A grain-like seed from a South American plant, eaten as a staple food.

emoji.text: A small digital image or icon used to express an idea or emotion.

podcast.text: A digital audio series that can be downloaded or streamed.

cyberspace.text: The notional environment in which communication over computer networks occurs.

selfie.text: A photograph one has taken of oneself, typically with a phone.

telegraph.text: A system for sending messages over a distance along a wire using coded signals.

zeppelin.text: A large rigid airship with a cylindrical body.

phonograph.text: An early device for recording and reproducing sound from cylinders or discs.

gramophone.text: A record player, especially an old hand-cranked one with a horn.

typewriter.text: A machine with keys for producing print-like characters on paper.

dirigible.text: An airship that can be steered.

velocipede.text: An early form of bicycle propelled by pushing along the ground or by pedals.

hovercraft.text: A vehicle that travels over land or water on a cushion of air.

spaceship.text: A spacecraft, especially one controlled by a crew.

robot.text: A machine capable of carrying out a complex series of actions automatically.

laser.text: A device that emits an intense, narrow beam of coherent light.

transistor.text: A semiconductor device used to amplify or switch electronic signals.

cholera.text: A bacterial infection of the small intestine, spread by contaminated water.

scurvy.text: A disease caused by a lack of vitamin C, historically common among sailors.

smallpox.text: A contagious viral disease with fever and pustules, now eradicated.

apothecary.text: A person who prepared and sold medicines and drugs.

phrenology.text: The discredited study of skull shape as supposedly indicative of character and ability.

mesmerism.text: A therapeutic system of hypnotic induction believed to involve animal magnetism.

alchemy.text: The medieval forerunner of chemistry, seeking to turn base metals into gold.

psychedelic.text: Relating to drugs that produce hallucinations; having vivid colors and swirling patterns.

cowabunga.text: Used to express delight or satisfaction; a surfer's cry.

tubular.text: Long, round, and hollow like a tube; (slang) excellent.

yuppie.text: A well-paid young middle-class professional with an affluent lifestyle.

beatnik.text: A young person associated with the countercultural Beat Generation.

hippie.text: A person of unconventional appearance associated with a subculture rejecting traditional values.

flapper.text: A fashionable young woman who flouted conventional standards of behavior.

bootlegger.text: A person who makes or sells alcohol illegally.

speakeasy.text: An illicit liquor store or bar during Prohibition.

hoodlum.text: A person who engages in crime and violence; a gangster.

cravat.text: A short, wide strip of fabric worn by men around the neck and tucked inside an open collar.

jalopy.text: An old car in a dilapidated condition.

gizmo.text: A gadget, especially one whose name is unknown.

blimp.text: A small airship without a rigid internal framework.

nylon.text: A tough, lightweight, elastic synthetic polymer used for fabrics.

bungalow.text: A low house with a single story.

suburbia.text: The suburbs and their inhabitants, viewed collectively.

chivalry.text: The medieval knightly system; courteous behavior, especially toward women.

scoundrel.text: A dishonest or unscrupulous person; a rogue.

sorcery.text: The use of magic, especially black magic.

unicorn.text: A mythical horse with a single horn; a startup company valued at over a billion dollars.

vampire.text: A corpse supposed to leave its grave at night to drink the blood of the living.

zombie.text: A corpse said to be revived by witchcraft; a person who is lifeless and apathetic.

werewolf.text: A person who changes into a wolf, typically at the full moon.

goblin.text: A mischievous, ugly, dwarf-like creature of folklore.

mermaid.text: A mythical sea creature with the head and upper body of a woman and the tail of a fish.

buccaneer.text: A pirate, originally one operating in the Caribbean.

cutlass.text: A short sword with a slightly curved blade, formerly used by sailors.

musket.text: An infantryman's light, long-barreled gun, typically smoothbore.

trebuchet.text: A medieval siege engine that hurls stones using a counterweight.

whimsical.text: Playfully quaint or fanciful, especially in an appealing way.

ephemeral.text: Lasting for a very short time.

mellifluous.text: (Of a voice or words) sweet or musical; pleasant to hear.

onomatopoeia.text: The formation of a word from a sound associated with what it names.

juggernaut.text: A huge, powerful, and overwhelming force or institution.

behemoth.text: A huge or monstrous creature; something enormous.

leviathan.text: A biblical sea monster; a very large aquatic creature or powerful state.

kraken.text: An enormous mythical sea monster said to appear off the coast of Norway.

yeti.text: A large, hairy creature said to live in the highest part of the Himalayas.

sasquatch.text: A large, hairy, humanlike creature reputed to live in North American forests; Bigfoot.

chupacabra.text: A legendary creature said to attack livestock and drink their blood.

dinosaur.text: A prehistoric reptile of the Mesozoic era; something outdated or obsolete.

pterodactyl.text: A prehistoric flying reptile with membranous wings.

hubbub.text: A chaotic din caused by a crowd of people.

humdinger.text: A remarkable or outstanding person or thing of its kind.

bugaboo.text: An object of fear or alarm; a bugbear.

boondoggle.text: Work or activity that is wasteful or pointless but gives the appearance of value.

hygge.text: A quality of coziness and comfortable conviviality (a Danish concept).

sriracha.text: A spicy sauce made from chili peppers, vinegar, garlic, sugar, and salt.

kombucha.text: A fermented, lightly effervescent sweetened tea drink.

turducken.text: A dish of a deboned chicken stuffed inside a duck stuffed inside a turkey.

flapjack.text: A pancake; (British) a sweet oat bar.

crumpet.text: A thick, flat, savory cake with a soft porous texture, eaten toasted.

marzipan.text: A sweet paste of ground almonds, sugar, and egg whites.

jambalaya.text: A Cajun dish of rice with shrimp, chicken, and spices.

sushi.text: A Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish or other toppings.

ketchup.text: A spicy sauce made chiefly from tomatoes and vinegar.

mayonnaise.text: A thick, creamy dressing made from egg yolks, oil, and vinegar.

spam.text: Canned pork luncheon meat; irrelevant or unsolicited messages sent over the internet.

software.text: The programs and other operating information used by a computer.

hashtag.text: A word or phrase preceded by a hash sign, used on social media to identify a topic.

steampunk.text: A genre of fiction with advanced machines powered by steam, often in a Victorian setting.

workaholic.text: A person who compulsively works excessively hard and long hours.

babysitter.text: A person who looks after a child or children while the parents are out.

cheeseburger.text: A hamburger with a slice of cheese on it.

supermarket.text: A large self-service store selling foods and household goods.
